title: "Week 3 Tutorial: Exploring Distributions"
subtitle: "Wednesday tutorial · reinforces Monday's lecture on EDA basics"
toc: true
---

## Goals

- Build a habit of exploring data visually *before* modeling it
- Practice the core `ggplot2` grammar: geoms, aesthetics
- Recognize skew and unequal variance by eye

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
data(iris)
iris <- as_tibble(iris)
```

## One numeric variable: distribution

```{r}
#| label: fig-hist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of sepal length"
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-density
#| fig-cap: "Density of sepal length by species"
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## One numeric + one categorical: comparing groups

```{r}
#| label: fig-box
#| fig-cap: "Sepal length by species"
ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Spotting problems before modeling

```{r}
iris |>
  group_by(Species) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Sepal.Length),
    sd = sd(Sepal.Length),
    skew_check = mean(Sepal.Length) - median(Sepal.Length)
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why this matters
A large gap between mean and median flags skew. Wildly different SDs
across groups flag unequal variance. Both affect which statistical
test is appropriate later in the course — EDA is where you catch
this *before* you're deep into modeling.
:::

## Exercises

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 1
For the built-in `ChickWeight` dataset, make a boxplot of final-day
weight by `Diet` (you'll need to `filter()` to the last time point
first). Does the spread look similar across diets?
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 2
For `PlantGrowth`, compare the mean-vs-median gap across the three
`group` levels the way we did for `iris` above. Do any groups look
notably skewed?
:::
